full_judgment: 8. In the present case the learned District Judge on consideration of the materials before him has come to the finding that the appellant-petitioner has been still functioning as the Chairman of Barisal Union Parisbad, cut by an order, dated 25.6.84 he has been unseated and the respondent-petitioner has not taken his office as yet. In these facts and circumstances, the learned District Judge, decided that unless status –quo is not maintained there will be complications afterward. So, I hold that the learned District Judge has exercised his discretion quite judiciously in the matter and has passed the order of stay in the exercise of his inherent jurisdiction under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of the above finding reference may be made if the case of Dilumuddin Madbar and others Vs. Province of East Pakistan and others reported in 21 DLR at page 569 wherein it has been held by Abdul Hakim, J. as follows: "In my opinion the Court has power to pass incidental order in such matters for the ends of justice if the circumstances so demand. Even if Order 9 Rule 13 C.P.C. does not confer any power upon the court the court is definitely vested with inherent power to meet the contingency and put off execution of the decree for some time to avoid duplication and multiplicity of litigations."
